en: The Section on the Training Rules (Sekhiyakaṇḍa)
The Chapter on the Propped-Up Position, 26.
The Training Rule on the Crossed Ankles.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six monks were sitting with their legs crossed inside a house...
[as before]. "The training is to be observed: 'I shall not sit with my legs crossed inside a house.
One must not sit with one's legs crossed inside a house."
Whoever, out of disrespect, sits in an inhabited area with his hands folded over his lap or with his robe folded over his lap, commits an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*).
There is no offense if it was unintentional.
In the case of one who is absent-minded, one who is unaware, or one who is ill.
For one who has entered upon the rains-retreat,
for one in times of distress, and for one who is insane.
The sixth training rule is concluded.
